A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Retro-Expert study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained image-based examples across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original USPTO-50K and ChemBench evaluations, ablations, automated and human reasoning assessments, and two laboratory syntheses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds USPTO-FULL and PaRoutes evaluations, training-policy comparisons, and further decision-space analyses.

M1.justification: The stated reasoning procedure changes from v1's global-to-local sequential subtask hierarchy to selective, autonomous use of candidate sets in v2 Section 3.4. The three-module architecture, selection/generation capabilities and overall KGPO framework remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds broader patent-reaction coverage through USPTO-FULL and full-route, multi-step retrosynthesis on PaRoutes. These extend the represented reaction distribution and task requirements beyond v1's coverage. USPTO-50K, ChemBench and the two laboratory synthesis targets are retained.

E2.justification: New reported comparators include GTA and EditRetro on USPTO-FULL, and DFPN, Retro*, MCTS and DMS-Deep on PaRoutes. Table 7 adds SFT and ordinary GRPO comparisons against KGPO. Conversely, RetroPrime's standalone and collaborative results disappear from Table 2, although it remains cited.

E3.justification: v2 adds Top-3/5/10 evaluation, with/without-decision-space controls, training-policy comparisons, candidate-count testing and an 80k-sample USPTO-FULL training setting. The stated default candidate count changes from three to four, although v1 already contains four-candidate prompts, leaving the earlier execution unclear. Figure 3 also changes its specialist context from GraphRetro to Graph2Edits.

E4.justification: New analyses test KGPO against SFT and GRPO (Table 7), the effect of supplying decision-space information to baseline LLMs (Table 9), and sensitivity to 1, 3, 4, 5 or 7 candidates (Table 10). The positional-shuffling analysis and successful-generation, selection and failure cases are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The three-evaluator human assessment and averaging procedure are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1's headline accuracy changes from 66.23% to 70.28%, and Figure 3's self-generation success changes from 46.2% to 40.6% alongside the specialist-context change; these do not establish same-setting gains or losses. Graph2Edits collaboration already scored 70.3% in v1 Table 2. New results include USPTO-FULL accuracy of 49.3%/63.0% at Top-1/3 and PaRoutes Top-1 accuracy of 38%. ChemBench, human evaluation and laboratory yields remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The stage-reward criterion changes from correct intermediate predictions to correct information contained in reasoning. New Figure 5 additionally illustrates two points for one stage, creating an inconsistency with v2's retained binary-reward definition in Equation 5. The candidate-space and policy-objective formulations otherwise remain, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit introductory claim that decision-space grounding enables RL without the conventional SFT prerequisite (Figure 1). The central claims of natural-language interpretability, specialist–LLM collaboration, plug-and-play compatibility and performance scaling remain essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting decision-space grounding to efficient exploration and interprets the new training-policy and candidate-count analyses. It removes v1's discussion that the human factual-correctness score of 3.69, versus GPT-4o's 3.89, indicates occasional factual errors. The appendix's site-discrimination and alternative-pathway limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents USPTO-FULL subset construction using reaction-pattern frequencies without ground-truth reaction-type labels, and adds a worked KGPO reward illustration. Training and baseline prompts receive limited refinements. Existing epoch count, completion limit, temperature, KL coefficient, reward weights and laboratory procedures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the new benchmark and planning comparisons, including PaRoutes, GTA, EditRetro and DirectMultiStep. It replaces the Yao et al. Retroformer agent-paper citation with Wan et al.'s retrosynthesis Retroformer paper. The related-work discussion largely retains its earlier positioning, with added emphasis on bypassing SFT before RL.

P1.justification: The methodology receives substantial rewriting, particularly the decision-space motivation, reasoning hierarchy and KGPO explanation. Experimental subsections are reorganized, and the appendix moves laboratory experiments and ablations ahead of case analyses and evaluation protocols. Numbered sections and revised terminology further change the document's organization.

P2.justification: v2 replaces Figure 1, redraws Figure 2, adds the KGPO illustration and redisplays laboratory reaction schemes in the main text. Tables gain decision-space indicators, Top-K columns and new comparisons. The appendix changes substantially to a two-column layout, with retained spectra, prompts and failure examples resized or rearranged.

improvement.justification: The new SFT/GRPO comparison and with/without-space controls strengthen evidence for KGPO and decision-space grounding beyond v1's supporting examples. USPTO-FULL and PaRoutes also test the retained generality claims more broadly. These benefits are tempered by incomplete settings for new experiments, the binary-reward versus Figure 5 inconsistency, and removal of the human factual-error qualification. The net improvement is supported but limited.
